title: WCL Asst. Foreman (Electrical) — Mock 12
pattern: WCL Asst. Foreman (Electrical) CBT (100 Q · 100 marks · 120 min · no −ve)

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A gas detector for methane (CH₄) in mines is calibrated to alarm at:
questions.solution: CH₄ alarm is set at 1% (alert) and 2% (danger, power cut-off).

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: CO (carbon monoxide) is dangerous in mines because:
options: It is odorless, colorless, and toxic — combines with hemoglobin
questions.solution: CO binds with hemoglobin 200–250× more strongly than O₂, causing asphyxiation.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: An oxygen deficiency alarm in mines is set to trigger below:
questions.solution: Below 19.5% O₂ is considered oxygen-deficient.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Electrical equipment in underground coal mines must be approved by:
questions.solution: Equipment must be tested and approved by DGMS-recognized testing laboratory.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The IS classification for electrical equipment in mines divides hazardous zones as:
options: Zone 0, 1, 2 for gas and Zone 20, 21, 22 for dust
questions.solution: IS/IEC 60079 classifies gas hazardous areas as Zone 0, 1, 2. Dust: 20, 21, 22.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Zone 0 in a gassy mine is defined as:
options: Area where explosive gas is present continuously or for long periods
questions.solution: Zone 0: explosive atmosphere present continuously or for long periods.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Zone 1 in a gassy mine is where:
options: Explosive gas atmosphere is likely to occur in normal operation
Gas may accumulate in abnormal conditions
questions.solution: Zone 1: explosive atmosphere likely during normal operations.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Zone 2 in a gassy mine is where:
options: Gas is likely during normal operation
Explosive gas atmosphere is not likely or occurs only briefly
questions.solution: Zone 2: abnormal conditions only, brief duration.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Portable gas detectors used in mines should be:
questions.solution: Daily bump test and regular calibration ensure detector reliability.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The flameproof category for underground coal mine equipment is:
questions.solution: Mining equipment requires Category 1 protection for Zone 0/1.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: An isolator in mine electrical system should be able to:
questions.solution: Isolators are off-load devices for visible isolation.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A circuit breaker in mine power system differs from an isolator because it can:
options: Make and break load and fault currents
questions.solution: CBs interrupt both normal load and fault currents.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The earth leakage relay (ELR) in mine electrical system detects:
options: Earth fault current by measuring CT residual current
questions.solution: ELR uses CBCT to detect residual current indicating earth fault.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A CBCT (Core Balance CT) for earth leakage protection works by:
options: Summing all phase and neutral currents — zero in healthy circuit
questions.solution: In healthy circuit, sum of all currents = 0. Earth fault causes imbalance.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The setting of earth leakage relay in coal mines is typically:
questions.solution: ELR in coal mines typically set at 300–500 mA.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: High-voltage equipment in underground mines requires an earth continuity monitor (ECM) to:
options: Continuously verify the integrity of earth continuity conductor
questions.solution: ECM verifies earth continuity conductor is intact. If broken, prevents starting.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The permissible touch voltage in mines under normal conditions is:
questions.solution: Permissible touch voltage is generally 55V AC.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Enclosed (dead-front) switchgear is preferred in mines because:
options: All live parts are enclosed, reducing accidental contact risk
questions.solution: Dead-front switchgear has no exposed live parts, reducing electrocution risk.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The main earthing conductor in a mine power system should have cross-section of:
options: At least half of the largest phase conductor
questions.solution: Main earthing conductor should be at least 50% of largest phase conductor.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Supplementary earth electrodes in mines are provided to:
options: Reduce earth electrode resistance for safety
questions.solution: Additional earth electrodes reduce overall earth resistance.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A 1000V insulation tester (megger) is used for testing MV cable insulation in mines at:
questions.solution: Megger applies 1000V DC to test MV cable insulation.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: As per the Mines Act 1952, women may be employed aboveground only between:
questions.solution: Mines Act 1952, s.46: women shall not be employed belowground, and aboveground employment is restricted between 6 a.m. and 7 p.m.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The maximum working hours in a week for an adult employed belowground in a mine are:
questions.solution: Mines Act 1952, s.28: no person shall be employed belowground for more than 48 hours in any week.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Re-energization after maintenance in mines requires:
options: Written authorization from the person who issued the permit to work
questions.solution: Only authorized person who issued PTW can authorize re-energization.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Under the Mines Act 1952, notice of which of the following accidents is required to be given to the prescribed authorities?
options: Loss of life, serious bodily injury, explosion, ignition, fire, inrush of water or other matter
questions.solution: Mines Act 1952, s.23: notice is required for loss of life, serious injury, and specified occurrences such as explosion, ignition, fire, inrush of water.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A switchgear room in an underground mine should have:
options: Adequate ventilation, fire-fighting equipment, and restricted access
questions.solution: Switchgear rooms need ventilation, fire protection, and access control.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Fire in a transformer oil can be extinguished by:
questions.solution: CO₂ and foam are effective for oil fires. Never use direct water on oil fires.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Emergency exit routes in underground mine electrical areas should be:
options: Clearly marked and illuminated at all times
questions.solution: Emergency exits must be clearly signed, well-lit, and free of obstructions.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Under the Mines Act 1952, an Inspector may, among other powers:
options: Enter, inspect and examine a mine, and make inquiries on any matter relating to safety
questions.solution: Mines Act 1952, s.22: Inspectors may enter, inspect, examine and inquire into any mine and its records.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Shot-firing cables in mines should be:
options: Insulated, dedicated cables separated from power cables
questions.solution: Shot-firing cables must be insulated and routed separately from power cables.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: An electrical earth in mines should be tested for resistance at least:
questions.solution: Earth electrode resistance should be tested at least annually.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: When workings approach within 60 m of a water body or waterlogged area, the manager shall:
options: Stop working immediately without any plan
Leave the water body untouched forever
Only mark it on the board
Prepare a scheme for protection against inrush and drain the water in a planned manner
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 149 (danger from surface water) & Ch. XI: within 60 m, protective schemes (drainage, barriers) are implemented.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Pilot wire monitoring in mine electrical system ensures:
options: Continuous checking of earth continuity conductor integrity
questions.solution: Pilot wire continuously monitors earth continuity. Any break triggers shutdown.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: An intrinsically safe circuit in mines means:
options: Circuit where energy stored is below the ignition threshold of surrounding gas
questions.solution: IS circuits limit energy below minimum ignition energy.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The Zener barrier in an intrinsically safe circuit:
options: Limits voltage and current to safe levels using Zener diodes
questions.solution: Zener barrier clamps voltage and limits current to safe levels.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Galvanic isolation for IS circuits is provided by:
questions.solution: Isolating transformers and opto-couplers provide galvanic isolation.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A safety shutdown system in mines should operate within:
options: Within seconds of detecting dangerous condition
questions.solution: Safety systems must actuate within seconds to prevent ignition.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The earthing system for mobile equipment in mines should be:
options: A trailing earth conductor connected before power conductor engages
questions.solution: Trailing earth must make contact first and break last.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Cable couplers in underground mines are flameproof and should:
questions.solution: Mine couplers are dead-break type — never operated under load.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A 11 kV cable in underground coal mine should have:
options: XLPE insulation with overall screen and earth screen
questions.solution: MV cables use XLPE insulation with metallic screens.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: In return airways and old workings, the air shall normally contain oxygen not less than ______ and carbon dioxide not more than ______.
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 165: not less than 19% oxygen and not more than 0.5% carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The maximum temperature of flameproof surface in Group I equipment is:
questions.solution: Surface temperature must stay below auto-ignition temperature of the gas.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Earth resistance of a main earth electrode in a mine substation should be:
questions.solution: Main earth electrode at mine substations should have resistance ≤ 5 ohms.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A 200 m trailing cable for a continuous miner should have how many earth conductors?
options: One earth conductor per phase conductor
questions.solution: Trailing cables have at least 2 dedicated earth conductors for redundancy.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Insulation resistance test on 11 kV mining cable should show a minimum of:
questions.solution: Acceptable IR for MV cables is ≥100 MΩ per km at 1000V DC.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The purpose of a circuit interlock in flameproof equipment is to:
options: Prevent opening of enclosure while circuit is live or under load
questions.solution: Interlocks prevent opening enclosure under live conditions.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Gas-proof enclosure for electrical equipment in mines means:
options: Enclosure that prevents entry of methane/air mixture into the equipment
questions.solution: Gas-tight enclosures prevent entry of explosive gas atmosphere.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The inspection interval for flameproof equipment in mines is:
options: Quarterly or as specified by DGMS
questions.solution: Flameproof equipment requires periodic inspection (typically quarterly).

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A flame path is defined as a:
options: Path through which gas from inside an enclosure can escape and be cooled
questions.solution: Flame path cools escaping hot gases below ignition temperature.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The maximum length of a flame path for Group IIA gas is:
questions.solution: For Group IIA: minimum flame path length 12.5 mm.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Which type of fire extinguisher is NOT suitable for electrical fires?
questions.solution: Water jet extinguishers are conductive and pose electrocution risk.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Emergency lighting in underground mine electrical installations should provide:
options: Minimum 1 lux on escape routes for at least 3 hours
questions.solution: Emergency lighting must illuminate escape routes at minimum 1 lux for 3 hours.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A rescue station in an underground mine should have:
options: Breathing apparatus, gas detectors, rescue equipment, and trained personnel
questions.solution: Rescue station equipped with SBA/SCBA, gas detection, and trained teams.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: If the percentage of inflammable gas in the general body of air exceeds ______, persons shall be withdrawn from the working.
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 166: persons are withdrawn when the general body of air exceeds 1.25% inflammable gas.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Electrical flash protection (arc flash) in mines can cause:
options: Severe burns, blast injury, and potential fatality from arc energy
questions.solution: Arc flash produces intense heat, UV radiation, pressure wave, and toxic fumes.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Approaching a goaf, probing shall be carried out ahead of the working for at least:
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 147: the working is probed ahead for at least 1.5 m beyond the last support before approaching the goaf.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: PPE for arc flash protection includes:
options: Flame-resistant clothing, face shield, and insulated gloves
questions.solution: Arc-rated clothing, face shield, insulated gloves, and leather boots required.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Electrical safety audit in mines should be conducted:
options: At least once a year by competent authority
questions.solution: Annual electrical safety audits by authorized inspectors ensure compliance.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: While driving approaching old or waterlogged workings, advance boreholes shall be kept at least ______ ahead of the face.
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 163: at least 3 advance boreholes not less than 3 m ahead of the face, with flank holes within 5 m on either side.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Every engine, motor, transformer and battery-charging room on the surface of a mine shall be provided with at least:
options: Two exits, properly maintained and kept free from obstruction
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 212: such rooms are kept clean and provided with at least two exits, properly maintained and free from obstruction.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Every mechanised outlet (shaft or incline) is examined at least once in every 7 days by:
options: An engineer, electrical supervisor or foreman, or a competent person authorised by the engineer
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 75(2): mechanised outlets are examined at least once in 7 days by an engineer, electrical supervisor or foreman (or authorised competent person), recorded in a bound paged book.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: In gassy mines, electric lighting from a source external to the lighting unit may be used on any roadway or place:
options: Ventilated by intake air or not within 270 m of the nearest face
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 176(1): external-source electric lighting is permitted on intake-air roadways or places not within 270 m of the nearest face.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The cutting motor of a continuous miner typically operates at:
questions.solution: Cutting motors operate at 415V AC or 550V DC depending on design.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A continuous miner cutter head is driven by:
options: Electric motor (AC or DC) through gear reduction
questions.solution: Electric motor drives cutting drum through gear reducer.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The electrical supply to a continuous miner in underground coal mine is typically through:
options: Trailing cable from a continuous miner transformer/starter
questions.solution: Power supplied through multi-core trailing cable from transformer and starter.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The trailing cable for a continuous miner has how many conductors?
questions.solution: Typical trailing cable: 3 power + 1 earth + 1 pilot + control pairs.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The pilot conductor in a mining trailing cable is used for:
options: Monitoring earth continuity and providing interlock
questions.solution: Pilot wire monitors earth continuity. If broken, starter trips.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A longwall shearer electrical system includes:
options: Haulage motors, cutting motors, and ranging arm motors with shearer controller
questions.solution: Shearer has multiple motors: drum cutting, haulage, and ranging arm motors.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The haulage system of a longwall shearer is powered by:
options: Electric motor with variable frequency drive (VFD)
questions.solution: Modern shearers use VFD-controlled haulage motors.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The power rating of a longwall shearer cutting motor is typically:
questions.solution: Shearer cutting motors are typically 200–500 kW each.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: SDL/LHD loaders in mines use which type of motor?
options: DC motor with SCR control or AC VFD
questions.solution: SDL/LHD use DC motors with SCR control or AC VFD in newer models.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The motor rating for an SDL (Side Dump Loader) is typically:
questions.solution: SDL motors range from 30–100 kW.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: An LHD (Load-Haul-Dump) machine is powered by:
options: Electric motor through trailing cable or battery
questions.solution: Electric LHDs use trailing cable. Battery LHDs use rechargeable packs.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Shot-firing circuits in mines use:
options: Dedicated shot-firing panel with safety interlocks
questions.solution: Shot-firing panels provide controlled, safe firing with safety interlocks.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The maximum voltage allowed for shot-firing in coal mines is:
questions.solution: Shot-firing circuits typically use ≤110V DC.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The blasting circuit in mines uses:
questions.solution: Series connection ensures uniform current through all detonators.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A galvanometer in shot-firing is used to:
options: Test continuity of the blasting circuit before firing
questions.solution: Exploder galvanometer tests circuit continuity using safe low current.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Cable management in mines requires cables to be:
options: Supported on insulators/hooks, away from water and traffic
questions.solution: Cables must be properly supported and protected from damage.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The maximum permissible current density for cables in mines depends on:
options: Insulation type, ambient temperature, and installation method
questions.solution: Current rating depends on insulation temperature limit, ambient, and grouping.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Underground mine lighting systems typically use:
questions.solution: Modern mine lighting uses LED or flameproof fluorescent luminaires.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: In what ratio must water be added to milk costing ₹30 per litre to get a mixture worth ₹20 per litre?

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: A train 150 m long passes a platform 100 m long in 15 seconds. What is the speed of the train?
questions.solution: Total distance = 250 m. Speed = 250/15 = 16.67 m/s = 60 km/h

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: A boat goes 20 km upstream in 5 hours and 20 km downstream in 2 hours. What is the speed of the current?
questions.solution: Upstream = 4 km/h, Downstream = 10 km/h. Speed of current = (10-4)/2 = 3 km/h

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: A train 200 m long crosses a pole in 20 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Statement: Some books are novels. All novels are interesting. Conclusion: Some books are interesting.
questions.solution: Some books are novels, all novels are interesting, so some books are interesting

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Number series: 5, 11, 17, 23, 29, ?:

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Statement: No fish is a bird. All birds can fly. Conclusion: No fish can fly.
questions.solution: Not all birds can fly (penguins, ostriches), so conclusion doesn't follow from premise

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: If SUN is coded as RUM, then MOON is coded as:
questions.solution: Each letter -1: S-1=R, U-1=T, N-1=M. M-1=L, O-1=N, O-1=N, N-1=M = LNNM

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Odd one out: India, China, Japan, Europe
questions.solution: Europe is a continent; others are countries

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Clock: Angle between hands at 9:15:
questions.solution: At 9:15: minute at 90°, hour at 277.5°, diff=157.5°

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Odd one out: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto
questions.solution: Pluto is dwarf planet; others are full planets

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Odd one out: Lion, Tiger, Leopard, Cheetah, Fox
questions.solution: Fox is smaller and from different family; others are big cats

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Statement: All flowers bloom. Some blooming things are beautiful. Conclusion: Some flowers are beautiful.
questions.solution: No definite connection between flowers and beautiful things

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Water is related to ice in the same way as milk is related to:
questions.solution: Water freezes to ice; milk curdles to curd

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Find the odd one: 125, 64, 27, 8, 1
questions.solution: All are perfect cubes: 5³,4³,3³,2³,1³

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: CIL stands for:
questions.solution: CIL = Coal India Limited

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: WCL stands for:
questions.solution: WCL = Western Coalfields Limited

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: NCL stands for:
questions.solution: NCL = Northern Coalfields Limited

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: CIL is a:
questions.solution: CIL: Miniratna (now Maharatna) PSU under Coal Ministry
